newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas sales.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended down on Tuesday from Monday's New York close on continuous selling, led by sales from Australia, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$327.60/328.10 per ounce on Tuesday, down from New York's US$328.50/25 per ounce on Monday.
"Steady sales from Australia pushed gold down to around $327.80 per ounce," said a dealer.
But overall volumes were thin ahead of U.S. economic indicators due for release later this week, sources said.
The United States is to release real gross domestic product figures for the second quarter on July 31.
Physical gold buying was thin as prices were still unattractive to buyers, dealers said.
"It's been a very quiet day, with physical prices going up," said one source.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to nil from its previous fix at -5.50.
Tael gold closed at HK$20 up at HK$3,033 per tael.
